source: #157 B3 stage-3 D-text (Fable 355419 Defect): the pi-durable same-id resume landed, but both entwurf_resume_call descriptions, its target parameter and the target-backend-unsupported visible-resume hint still named only pi and Claude Code. Provenance, not blended with any earlier layer's: Opus 169dd1 copied the old values from the 46c7c776 worktree Root text and wrote the new literals in the same pass, before the producer edit; they were NOT approved before it, and their independent review is Fable's, which follows, like revisions 12 and 16. The MCP description stays within the 2048-character host cap.

amendments.old: Only on an explicit operator request, reopen ONE DORMANT pi or Claude Code citizen under its OWN garden id, in a visible window in the operator's own tmux session — or, for pi inside herdr, a new herdr tab. The record supplies everything — which session, which cwd, and for pi which transcript, model and provider — so the only input is the target id: there is no model override, no task, and no prompt, and a Claude Code session comes back as `claude --resume <its session id>` with none of the model or permission flags it was once started with. This verb submits NO prompt; what the runtime itself does after it comes back (for Claude Code, its hook re-arms the doorbell and unread mail may then wake a turn) is not measured, and talking to it is still entwurf_v2 fire-and-forget. You get TWO receipts and they mean different things: a LAUNCH receipt (tmux made a window, or herdr a tab, and was asked to start the runtime) and an OBSERVATION receipt (pi: the control socket answered under the same id; Claude Code: a NEW live process in the window this call opened re-armed its receiver marker for the same session with a fresh arm binding the record also carries; or resume-unobserved; or record-unreadable with its cause). Unobserved is a real outcome, not an error to retry — the window is visible, so read it. A citizen that is already LIVE is refused: address it with entwurf_v2 instead. A Claude Code citizen is reopened only when the last validated owner the Entwurf hook armed for its session is proven gone AND that arm is still the record's last one; no marker, an unreadable or mismatched one, an inconclusive owner or an unbound one is refused, and a process holding the session without a committed hook attach is invisible to that proof. Other backends have no same-id resume. Requires that this agent itself runs inside tmux, or inside herdr for a pi target only (a Claude Code target is refused there, never sent to tmux).

You get TWO receipts and they mean different things: a LAUNCH receipt (tmux made a window, or herdr a tab, and was asked to start the runtime) and an OBSERVATION receipt (pi: the control socket answered under the same id; pi-durable: the child it started adopted this call's reservation; Claude Code: a NEW live process in the window this call opened re-armed its receiver marker for the same session with a fresh arm binding the record also carries; or resume-unobserved; or record-unreadable with its cause). amendments.old: Only on an explicit operator request, reopen ONE dormant pi or Claude Code citizen under its own garden id in a visible tmux window — or, for pi inside herdr, a new herdr tab — through the entwurf-bridge (target required; the record supplies the session and cwd — no task or prompt is submitted). Returns the bridge's LAUNCH and OBSERVATION receipts or its named refusal: a live target, another backend, or a Claude Code citizen not proven dormant is refused by name, and opening it needs the tmux session — or, for pi only, the herdr pane — this host itself was launched in; a Claude Code target inside herdr is refused, never sent to tmux. Existing unread mail may still wake the resumed runtime; neither receipt proves what it did.
